tts_summary: Here's what you need to know from the afternoon note on September 29th, 2026. This one is focused entirely on OpenAI's Dev Day keynote, which wrapped in under 60 minutes — and Adam gives them credit for that. Let's get into the takeaways. The headline product was something called Dots, OpenAI's new personal AI agent. The key point here is that Dots is squarely aimed at enterprise and professional users, not everyday consumers. That is a meaningful distinction. Meta's consumer AI product, Muse, is a very different animal, and Adam sees the Dots announcement as a relief for Meta rather than a threat. On the broader product side, OpenAI also launched GPT-5.1 Sol — described as near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth the cost — and a new model called Ultrafast, which offers up to eight times faster token generation in Codex and up to six times faster through the API. Those are not incremental updates. Now for the numbers, because they matter. Weekly GPT users are now at one point two billion, up from roughly one billion over the summer. An Axios report out earlier in the day said annual recurring revenue is approaching seventy billion dollars. And Bloomberg reported OpenAI is looking to raise at least thirty billion dollars in a new funding round at a valuation of one point four trillion dollars. That is a staggering number. Adam's number one takeaway is clear: Dots is not a Muse killer. The two products are targeting different users in different contexts. The second and arguably more important strategic read is what this means for Anthropic. OpenAI has been on a significant momentum run since the Astra launch, recapturing market share and mindshare. And it is probably not a coincidence that Anthropic's IPO has been pushed out during exactly that same window. OpenAI's resurgence is making it harder for competitors to tell a differentiated story to public market investors. Bottom line for traders: watch Meta as a potential beneficiary here given the consumer versus enterprise split. The Anthropic IPO delay is worth monitoring as a broader signal of how capital is concentrating in the AI space. No macro or Fed commentary in this note — this was a pure AI competitive dynamics update.
